paragraphs.text: DeepSeek Harness bundle: a Settings row that opens the harness home's AGENTS.md ($DSH_HOME, else ~/.
dsh) in your system editor.
# AGENTS.md Settings Row — DeepSeek Harness

DeepSeek Harness reads `AGENTS.md` on every new session, but its UI has no way to
*open* that file.

This small bundle adds one row to **Settings → General** that hands
the file to your editor.
中文说明见文末。
## What it does

Clicking **用记事本打开 / Open in editor** opens the user-global `AGENTS.md` of the
harness home — `%DSH_H

OME%\AGENTS.md`, or `~/.dsh/AGENTS.md` when `DSH_HOME` is
unset. Nothing else: no telemetry, no netw
ork, no changes to the file itself.

On Windows the bundle launches **Notepad** directly. A `.md` file usually has no shell
association,

so relying on "open with the default app" would show a picker (or do
nothing at all when started thr
ough `cmd /c start`).
## How it works
A cordis bundle with a host half and a client half:
| File | Role |

| `cordis.patch.yml` | inserts one row named `agents-md-settings` into the profile |
| `index.js` |
host: resolves the harness home, registers `GET /agents-md/path` and `POST /agents-md/open`, launche

s the editor |
| `client.js` | client: registers the row into the `settings.general.item` slot |
| `
package.json` | `dsh.bundle.patch` and `dsh.client` declarations |

The client reads `/agents-md/path` on mount and posts to `/agents-md/open` on click.
The host resolv

es `$DSH_HOME/AGENTS.md`, falling back to `~/.dsh/AGENTS.md`, then
launches an editor — `notepad.exe

` on Windows, `open` on macOS, `xdg-open` elsewhere.
On Windows it then waits for the Notepad window

, restores it, sizes it to 900×640 and
raises it, because a stale saved window placement can make an

opened file look like
nothing happened.

Neither route takes a body or a caller-supplied path, so the only file they can ever
touch is the cu
rrent user's own `AGENTS.md`.
## Install

This is a bundle, not an npm-published plugin. Use the profile the app actually runs —
on Windows de

sktop it defaults to `%ProgramData%\dsh-data\profiles\desktop`; the exact
path is in the app's `DSH_

ults to `%ProgramData%\dsh-data\profiles\desktop`; the exact
path is in the app's `DSH_PROFILE_DIR`.

**Install it as a plugin. Never copy the folder into `node_modules`.** A copied folder
is pruned by

the next `pnpm install`, and every plugin install or upgrade runs one —
that is how this bundle can

disappear on its own while the patch row that points at it
stays behind. An installed package is a r
ecorded dependency, so later installs keep it.
### As a package (recommended)

The same string works in the app: **Settings → Plugins → Add plugin**, which accepts a
package name,

a Git address, a tarball or an absolute local path. The installer writes
the dependency into `<prof

ile>/package.json` and applies the bundle's own patch row, so
later installs leave it alone. Restart

DeepSeek Harness; the row appears at the bottom
of **Settings → General**.

If the row is missing after a restart, the patch row did not get applied — add it by
hand as shown u
nder *From a local checkout* below.

If your build exposes the `plugin_manager` tool, `install_bundle` with

his checkout>"` does steps 1–3 for you.
## Uninstall

Uninstall through the same surface: **Settings → Plugins** removes the package and its
patch row. By

hand, drop the `@local/agents-md-settings` dependency from
`<profile>/package.json` and the `agents

-md-settings` insert row from
`<profile>/cordis.patch.yml`, run `pnpm install --dir <profile>` so th

e folder is
cleaned up, and restart.
## Notes and limitations

- **Edits take effect on the next session.** `AGENTS.md` is read once, at the first
request of a ses

sion, and is not watched for external changes.
- **The path follows `DSH_HOME`.** The instruction lo

ader reads `$DSH_HOME/AGENTS.md`,
or `~/.dsh/AGENTS.md` when the variable is unset; this row resolve

s the same way. A
hard-coded `~/.dsh` would silently edit an unread file on every machine that moved

its harness home to another drive, a portable install, or a shared directory.
- **One file of two.*

* The loader also reads `$DSH_AGENTS_HOME/AGENTS.md`
(`~/.agents/AGENTS.md` by default). This row ed

its only the harness-home file.
- **Windows only for now**, tested on Windows 11 with the desktop ap

p. macOS and Linux
use `open` / `xdg-open` but are untested.
- The route listens on the app's own lo

cal origin. It opens one fixed file and accepts
no arguments; it is not a general-purpose "run this"

endpoint.
- If the row does not appear, check that the package resolved and that
`cordis.patch.yml`

still parses; a YAML typo prevents the whole patch layer from
loading.
## Version history
| Version | Change |
| 1.0.3 | Resolve the harness home (`$DSH_HOME`, else `~/.dsh`) instead of hard-coding `~/.dsh`, and
add `GET /agents-md/path` so the row shows the file it will open. A moved home used to make the row

edit a file no session read. |
| 1.0.2 | README: lead with `dsh plugin add github:…` so a new user
installs a real package instead of copying the folder into `node_modules` and losing it on the next

install. |
| 1.0.1 | README: install as a profile dependency. A folder copied into `node_modules` is

deleted by the next `pnpm install`, which is why the row could vanish on its own. |
| 1.0.0 | Works

end to end on Windows. Client posts to the route; host launches Notepad and raises its window. |
